text:
For Tatiana, my first daughter


The day is gray
and my hands are cold
when through the
        window
I see the rosebushes shaking
in the garden
lashed by the
        wind.
It begins to rain
like a slow apprenticeship
of
        nature
until the darkness
that has been growing
enters
        my spirit.
I hear a slight
sigh
behind me
and I
        turn around
seeking to recover the time
of joy
in the exact
        space
occupied by the small
animated bundle
on the rug.

        In her pale face I see myself repeated
and I think that smile of hers

        innocent
is capable of moving the world
in which I move

        lighting it
until it clips the wings
of sadness
and restores
        a thousand times
the genuine face
of peace.

translation.title: Smile
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's domestic turn from gray weather into the child's restorative smile.
